subject: Architecture review & migration PoC — scheduling
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acmeai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Architecture review and migration PoC — request

Hi Soojin,

We spent this week evaluating Redwood's benchmark notes vs our current self-hosted stack and would like to schedule a technical deep-dive to discuss a migration PoC. Primary goals are: (1) validate latency/cost tradeoffs for our 13B+ models, (2) understand prefix/KV caching behavior with our multi-tenant prompts, and (3) review network/topology implications for our VPC setup.

Attendees from our side: Lina Gomez (ML Platform), Rajiv Patel (Infra/Networking).

Can you propose 2–3 slots next week for a 45–60 minute session? We prefer late-morning PST. Also would appreciate a short agenda so we can prep (we can share infra specs ahead of time).

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of ML Platform, AcmeAI
amit.shah@acmeai.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@acmeai.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Architecture review and migration PoC — request

Hi Amit / Lina —

Thanks for the note. Ben (SE) and Dev (Solutions Eng) are copied — they'll run the technical deep-dive. Proposed slots (PST):

- Tue 9/15 10:00–11:00am
- Tue 9/15 1:30–2:30pm
- Wed 9/16 11:00–12:00pm

Suggested 60-minute agenda (attached):
- 5m intros & PoC goals
- 15m current infra + model/workload snapshot (you)
- 25m Redwood runtime deep-dive (serving runtime, caching, quantization)
- 10m next steps / commit checklist

I've attached a short agenda and example environment snapshot format — if you can drop your infra notes in the Confluence link (or attach them), that will help us tailor the session.

If none of the slots work, tell us 2 windows that do and we'll adjust.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

Amit —

Quick note on the prep items that will make the deep-dive highest value:
- model family and sizes (13B / 33B / etc), typical prompt/sequence length distribution
- expected concurrent requests per-minute and p99 latency target
- any existing KV cache / prefix usage patterns
- current infra diagram (VPC subnets, NAT/GW details)

If you can drop a one-page diagram, that helps — I attached an example topology we usually request for PoCs (screenshot).

Also, when we run the session we'll show a short live trace: how we route requests (hosted vs dedicated), where fallback/quantization would happen, and what metrics to watch during the PoC (tokens/s, GPU utilization, tail latency).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

We'll upload an infra snapshot to the Confluence page by end of day Monday. Can you make the agenda explicit about KMS/VPC items?
